Place \(AE\) on the \(x\)-axis with  
\[
A=(0,0),\qquad E=(20,0).

Since \(\angle A=\angle E=90^\circ\), the sides \(AB\) and \(DE\) are both perpendicular to \(AE\).  
Because \(B,C,D\) are on the same side of line \(AE\), take \(y>0\).  Write
\[
B=(0,s),\qquad D=(20,t)
\]
where \(s=AB\) and \(t=DE\).

---

### 1.  Locating \(C\)

At \(B\), \(\angle B=45^\circ\).  Ray \(BA\) points down, so ray \(BC\) makes a \(45^\circ\) angle with it toward the interior (right side of the clockwise pentagon).  
Thus \(BC\) has slope \(-1\).

Since \(BC=14\sqrt2\),
\[
\Delta x=\Delta y = 14\sqrt2\cdot \frac{\sqrt2}{2}=14.
\]
Hence
\[
C=(14,s-14).
\]
For \(C\) to be on the same side of \(AE\) as \(B\), we need \(s>14\).

The interior angle at \(C\) is \(540^\circ-(90+45+45+90)=270^\circ\).  
So the exterior angle is \(90^\circ\).  The direction of \(BC\) is \(-45^\circ\); turning left by \(90^\circ\) gives direction \(+45^\circ\) for \(CD\).

Thus \(CD\) has slope \(+1\).  Since \(D\) lies on the line \(x=20\), the horizontal gap from \(C\) to \(D\) is \(20-14=6\).  Hence
\[
\Delta y = 6,\qquad CD=6\sqrt2,
\]
and
\[
D=(20,\;s-14+6)=(20,s-8).
\]
So
\[
t=DE=s-8.
\]

Indeed \(t>0\) because \(s>14\), and \(t<s\) automatically.

---

### 2.  Area in terms of \(s\)

The vertices are
\[
(0,0),\;(0,s),\;(14,s-14),\;(20,s-8),\;(20,0).
\]

Using the shoelace formula (or integrating the upper boundary):
\[
\begin{aligned}
\text{Area}
&=\int_0^{14}(s-x)\,dx+\int_{14}^{20}(x+s-28)\,dx\\
&=14s-98+(6s-66)\\
&=20s-164.
\end{aligned}
\]

### 3.  Congruence condition

\[
20s-164\equiv 4s-4\equiv 0\pmod{16}

\]

s\in\{17,21,25,\dots,2025\}.
